meta.case_name: Pharma Company Goes International, Outsources Benefits, Integrates New Technology

prompt.context: Waltham&Rose, a pharmaceutical company based and solely operational in the US, has recently announced its imminent international expansion to Germany and France. The company will be increasing its employee numbers by 50% as a result of this expansion. To ease workloads and minimize complexity during this growth phase, Waltham&Rose executives are strongly considering outsourcing health benefits management. Executives have also decided to, for the first time, integrate a cloud-based CRM software, which all employees (many of whom have worked for Waltham&Rose for decades) will be required to use. Waltham&Rose has sought out Deloitte Human Capital to develop and help implement a seamless CRM technology adoption process, and to help ensure new Europe-based employees feel they are a part of the Waltham&Rose 'family,' and represent the brand well. The pharma industry has become increasingly competitive in recent years, with peer companies having already invested significantly in global expansion and technological advancements. Waltham&Rose executives feel they have no time to waste in implementing the above changes.
prompt.question: Waltham&Rose has engaged Deloitte Human Capital to help manage this complex transformation. How would you structure your approach to help the client successfully expand internationally, outsource health benefits management, and integrate a new CRM technology across their workforce?

clarifying_info.q: Are any Waltham&Rose senior executives planning to relocate to Europe?
clarifying_info.a: There have been some discussions about this, but as yet there is no firm plan for any senior executive to relocate.

clarifying_info.q: Since the company has operated purely domestically for decades, do they have any in-house expertise about European business regulations?
You mentioned that some employees have worked for Waltham&Rose for decades – what is the demographic breakdown of their workforce overall, in terms of age in particular?
clarifying_info.a: It is largely people in their forties and fifties, most of whom have worked for the company for at least 10 years.

clarifying_info.q: Is there already a plan in place for outsourcing the healthcare benefits?
clarifying_info.a: No – and outsourcing is new territory for Waltham&Rose.

framework: Business Issues: Acquisition/Expansion Management and Workforce Stabilization

Work Stream 1 – Organizational/Gap Analysis: Assess (job design, change readiness assessment) → Implement (predictive competency modeling, revamped job descriptions, new roles such as Outsourcing Manager/CRM Manager/International Compliance Manager, recruitment strategy, hiring and training timeline) → Evaluate (progress against strategy and timeline, individual job performance)

Work Stream 2 – Training and Learning: Assess (current training opportunities, type of learning organization, stakeholder/learning-persona analysis) → Implement (training and learning strategy, multiple content-consumption formats aligned to learning personas, rationalized curricula, rewards system) → Evaluate (pace of learning, adoption rate, knowledge retention, user feedback)

Work Stream 3 – Technology Adoption: Assess (technology impact assessment, CRM accessibility outside office network, data-migration costs for CRM and healthcare) → Implement (technology adoption and transition plan, consistent communication on timeline and benefits, contingency plan) → Evaluate (employee acceptance, usage rates, reductions in manual workarounds, cost savings)
Other Considerations: change management, communications strategy, talent pipeline, employee engagement and culture, dependencies between work streams, top-line/bottom-line impact of each work stream

questions.prompt: Why did you prioritize these three work streams?
questions.guidance: Candidate should explain that organizational/gap analysis is foundational because you cannot train or adopt technology before understanding role requirements and headcount needs. Training and learning comes next because a largely tenured, older workforce will need structured support for CRM adoption. Technology adoption is third because it depends on both the organizational design and the training strategy being in place. Candidate should also reference the urgency the client feels given competitive dynamics.

questions.prompt: If Waltham&Rose can only afford to prioritize one work stream initially, which would you choose and why?
questions.guidance: Organizational/gap analysis is the most defensible first choice because it unblocks everything else — you cannot hire, train, or adopt technology without first knowing who you need and what competencies are required. Candidate should acknowledge trade-offs and explain how the remaining work streams would be phased in once budget allows.

questions.prompt: In this case, how could you set the stage for additional business opportunities later on?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify opportunities to expand scope: building an ongoing change management practice, creating a long-term learning center or L&D function for the client, running a follow-on engagement for performance management post-expansion, or leveraging Deloitte's affiliate research partners. Candidate should frame this as building a long-term client relationship.

questions.prompt: What is the biggest risk with the plan you laid out and how will you minimize it?
questions.guidance: Strong answers identify employee resistance (especially from tenured, older employees) to CRM adoption and outsourcing of healthcare as the biggest risk, given the demographic profile. Mitigation tactics include early stakeholder communication, piloting the CRM rollout before global launch, providing multiple training formats (video, nano-learning, classroom) to match different learning personas, and ensuring healthcare outsourcing transition is transparent and frictionless.

questions.prompt: Waltham&Rose has expressed reluctance to invest in training. How will you address this?
questions.guidance: Candidate should make the business case: employee engagement is a key driver of profitability; poor CRM adoption leads to manual workarounds and lost productivity; reskilling current employees is cheaper than attrition and rehiring. Link training investment to top-line and bottom-line outcomes. Also note that the competitive environment (peer companies already invested in global expansion and technology) makes under-investment in training a strategic risk.

brainstorming.prompt: You identified several types of training methodologies Waltham&Rose could utilize. Is it really necessary to have so many different approaches? Also, Waltham&Rose does not have a plan for who will lead the new offices in France and Germany — what are your thoughts? Additionally, you focused a lot on CRM adoption but did not discuss the outsourcing of health benefits much — can you expand on that?

categories.name: Multiple training methodologies justification
ideas: The employee base spans a wide age range — US employees are largely in their 40s–50s; European hires may skew younger, creating different learning styles
Research shows different age groups absorb content at different rates and through different modalities
Some employees prefer self-paced learning (video reference) over classroom settings
With employees across multiple countries and time zones, diverse formats ensure equitable access
CRM adoption in particular requires accommodating varying levels of tech comfort
Formats to consider: nano-learning, video modules, game-based learning, train-the-trainer (TOT), classroom sessions

categories.name: Leadership for European offices
ideas: At least one senior US executive should relocate to each new office, at least for the medium term, to preserve company culture and ensure cohesion
Extensive involvement of the HR Director will be critical during the transition
US executives should be balanced with senior German and French hires to ease cultural friction, address language barriers, and leverage local regulatory knowledge
Local senior hires signal commitment to the new markets and help attract talent

categories.name: Outsourcing health benefits
ideas: Waltham&Rose is new to outsourcing — the transition will require careful change management to prevent employee anxiety
Unclear or poorly communicated changes to healthcare benefits negatively affect employee performance and engagement
Healthcare regulations differ significantly between the US, Germany, and France — multiple outsourcing partners may be required
Employees must have a clear, accessible point of contact for their new benefits manager
Communication strategy around healthcare changes should be proactive and transparent
Contingency plan needed if outsourcing partner underperforms or if regulatory issues arise in Europe

recommendation: Structure the engagement around three prioritized work streams: (1) Organizational/Gap Analysis, (2) Training and Learning, and (3) Technology Adoption — executed in phases of Assess, Implement, and Evaluate
Prioritize the organizational gap analysis first as it is foundational to all downstream activities
Pilot the CRM adoption training in the US before global rollout to identify friction points
Engage European local senior hires alongside relocated US executives to balance culture and local knowledge
Use multiple training formats tailored to the older, tenured US workforce and the incoming European employees

Proactively communicate healthcare outsourcing changes to avoid employee anxiety and performance drops; confirm whether one or multiple outsourcing partners are needed given different regulatory environments in the US, Germany, and France
risks: Resistance to CRM from a largely older, long-tenured workforce
Regulatory non-compliance in Germany and France due to lack of in-house European expertise
Employee anxiety and disengagement during the healthcare outsourcing transition
No senior executive committed to relocate, risking culture gaps in European offices
Compressed timeline due to competitive urgency increases execution risk across all three work streams
next_steps: Conduct all-hands half-day workshop to accelerate gap and change-readiness assessment
Identify and begin recruitment for Outsourcing Manager, CRM Manager, and International Compliance Manager roles
Select and begin contracting with healthcare benefits outsourcing partners (likely separate US and European vendors)
Design pilot CRM training program and select cohort for US pilot
Establish governance structure and communication cadence for the transformation program
